The '''Genassa system''' was located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim's]] [[M'shinni sector/Legends|M'shinni sector]] and contained six [[Planet/Legends|planets]], including [[Genassa/Legends|Genassa]]. Genassa's [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[M'shinn]] [[Species/Legends|species]] [[Terraforming/Legends|terraformed]] the rest of the [[Star system/Legends|system's]] planets before eventually expanding to other systems. The Genassa system eventually became a part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], before ultimately being [[Yuuzhan Vong War|conquered]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extragalactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] species.

==Description==
The Genassa system was a part of the [[M'shinni sector/Legends|M'shinni sector]]<ref name="EAOC" /> in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It contained six [[Planet/Legends|planets]], including<ref name="GG12" /> the terrestrial<ref name="Mask">''[[Mask of the Pirate Queen]]''</ref> world<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|330|Genassa}}</ref> [[Genassa/Legends|Genassa]] that was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by a [[Genassa's moon|large moon]].<ref name="GG12" />

==History==
[[File:Mshinni.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The M'shinn species was native to the Genassa system's planet of the same name.]]
At some point, population pressures on Genassa forced its [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[M'shinn]] [[Species/Legends|species]] to [[Colonist/Legends|colonize]] outer [[Realspace/Legends|space]], beginning with the construction of [[orbital biosphere]]s and then proceeding with the settlement of Genassa's [[Moon/Legends|moon]] and the [[Terraforming/Legends|terraforming]] of the rest of the Genassa [[Star system/Legends|system's]] planets. Eventually,<ref name="GG12" /> at some point by [[3966 BBY/Legends|3966 BBY]],<ref name="MshinniInterstellar">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'' establishes that the [[Skrilling/Legends|Skrillings]] first traveled off-world after the [[M'shinn]]i had [[Colonist/Legends|colonized]] their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] [[Agriworld-2079/Legends|Agriworld-2079]]&mdash;which ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places in a [[Agriworld-2079 system/Legends|star system]] other than the Genassa [[Star system/Legends|system]]. The ''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]'' establishes that [[Jervo Thalien]]&mdash;whom [[Knights of the Old Republic 1|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 1]] depicts as a Skrilling&mdash;was [[Chairman/Legends|chairman]] of the off-world company [[Lhosan Industries]] by the time [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] became a member [[Planet/Legends|world]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Since ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' dates the latter event to [[3966 BBY/Legends|3966 BBY]], the M'shinni must have therefore acquired interstellar travel ability at some point by that date.</ref> the M'shinni developed a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], which allowed them to colonize hundreds of worlds in the M'shinni [[Sector/Legends|sector]].<ref name="GG12" />

Space surrounding the Genassa system was explored by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] between [[3000 BBY]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], and the system was situated within the borders of the Republic by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="TEA" /> During the first campaigns of the Clone Wars in 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the [[Ninth Army]] of the Republic was tasked with engaging the [[Confederacy military/Legends|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in the Genassa system's vicinity.<ref name="EGTW" /> Shortly after the acquisition of the planet [[Ukio/Legends|Ukio]] by the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] during that conflict, the Genassa system was featured on a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Map/Legends|map]] displayed on a [[Viewscreen/Legends|viewscreen]] at a facility run by [[Passel Argente/Legends|Passel Argente]], the [[Magistrate/Legends|Magistrate]]<ref name="AoI">''[[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct]]''</ref> of the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]].<ref name="DB Argente">{{DB|character|passelargente|Argente, Passel}}</ref>

The system was incorporated into the territory of the Galactic Empire by [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]].<ref name="EGTW" /> By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], [[Starship/Legends|starships]] frequently emerged from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] for [[Navigator/Legends|navigational]] calculations in an isolated region of space between Genassa and the [[Bright Jewel sector/Legends|Bright Jewel sector]] planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]].<ref name="Mask" /> By [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], the Genassa system had become a part of the Empire's eventual successor state, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="EGTW" /> [[27 ABY/Legends|Fourteen years]] later, the system had been conquered by the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extragalactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] species as part of its [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. It remained under the invaders' [[Yuuzhan Vong empire|control]] until [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
Genassa was the homeworld of the sentient M'shinn species.<ref name="GG12" /> Around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the population of the Genassa system numbered between one and ten billion.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The star system containing Genassa was first mentioned in the [[1995]] [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'', in an entry authored by [[Lisa Smedman]].<ref name="GG12" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]] identified the Genassa system by name and placed it in grid square M-7.<ref name="TEA" /> ''[[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct]]'', a [[Star Wars comic books|webcomic]] authored by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and released on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="AoI" /> over the span of the 2009<ref name="AoI announcement">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20091001comics/index.html|text=New ''Clone Wars'' Web Comic Tells Original Tale}}</ref>&ndash;[[2010]]<ref name="Lethal Trackdown Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode222.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Lethal Trackdown}}</ref> [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series,<ref name="AoI announcement" /> featured the first appearance of the system.<ref name="AoI" />

[[File:GenassaOnCelanonSpur-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A number of maps of the galaxy published in several ''Star Wars'' sources placed the Genassa system on the Celanon Spur.]]
In ''The Essential Atlas'', a number of galactic maps depict the system between the [[Bright Jewel system/Legends|Bright Jewel]] and [[Ottega system/Legends|Ottega systems]] on the [[Celanon Spur/Legends|Celanon Spur]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace route]].<ref name="TEA" /> That placement of the Genassa system was later repeated in several maps in other sources.<ref name="EGTW" /><ref name="EotECR">[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire'' Core Rulebook]]</ref><ref name="FF">''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File Collector's Guide & Galaxy Chart]]''</ref><ref name="Podracing">{{SW|url=news/this-is-podracing-sports-in-the-star-wars-galaxy-part-1|series=Sports in the Star Wars Galaxy|text=Part 1: This Is Podracing|nolive=1}}</ref><ref name="AoRCR">[[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]]</ref><ref name="FDCR">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> However, in a map of ''The Essential Atlas'' focusing on the Genassa system's galactic region, the Mid Rim, it is instead placed a relatively short distance off that segment of the Celanon Spur<ref name="TEA" />&mdash;a placement that was also repeated in the StarWars.com [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the book<ref name="Mid Rim">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-sectors-of-the-mid-rim|text=Essential Atlas Extra: Sectors of the Mid Rim}}</ref> as well as in a smaller-scale map in Jason Fry and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]'s [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' focusing on the Genassa system's galactic neighborhood. This article assumes that the placement originating from these latter, more specific maps is correct.<ref name="EGTW" />

[[File:OrdMantellIthor25ABY-TEA.png|thumb|left|300px|''The Essential Atlas'' depicted several forces traveling through the Genassa system during the Yuuzhan Vong War.]]
Furthermore, ''The Essential Atlas'' depicts the military forces of three galactic factions transiting the Genassa system while traveling along the Celanon Spur during the Yuuzhan Vong War in 25 ABY&mdash;namely, New Republic forces and later those of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] pass through the system while traveling [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Rimward]], and subsequently the forces of the Yuuzhan Vong transit the system while advancing [[Core Worlds/Legends|Coreward]].<ref name="TEA" /> Similarly, ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' depicts a [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdout]] force traveling through the Genassa system while fleeing Coreward in the aftermath of the [[Ciutric Offensive]] of the Imperial [[Reconquest of the Rim]] in 19 BBY. In line with the prior assumption, this article assumes that, while the abovelisted forces did travel along the Celanon Spur, they did not, in fact, pass through the Genassa system.<ref name="EGTW" />
